title: Shot list and framing
purpose: Describes what kinds of shots and visual assets appear, how large the subject is, where negative space is left for text, and what an author must supply per item.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: One F1 frame per shot (or the keyframe), F3 crops to judge sharpness, F10 to find reused images.
pitfalls: Labelling shot scale on a still graphic with no subject
Assuming a source is stock footage from look alone
Missing reused images because they are zoomed differently

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F4: Whole-video contact sheet, 1 frame per second: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=1,scale=180:-2,tile=8x8" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/sheet.jpg" (or use the keyframes and contact sheet from video_re_keyframes_contact_sheet)
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"

questions.question: What is the distribution of shot types (extreme close-up, close-up, medium, wide, insert/detail, screen capture, graphic-only card)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills subject_framing and the shot mix the renderer plans.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify each shot keyframe (evidence.shots[].keyframe or F4 sheet) into one type; report counts and shares.
questions.challenge: Re-classify 6 random shots blind; disagreements over one step of scale are tolerable, two steps are not.

questions.question: How large is the main subject as a fraction of frame height, median across shots?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets subject scale for asset placement.
questions.how_to_answer: On 8 sampled keyframes measure the subject's bounding box height in pixels / source.height.
questions.challenge: Shots without a clear subject must be excluded and counted in the note.

questions.question: Is the subject placed centrally, on a rule-of-thirds line, or offset toward one side?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the subject placement rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the subject centre x/width ratio on sampled keyframes.
questions.challenge: Report the measured x ratios; 'centre' needs most within 0.42-0.58.

questions.question: How much headroom is left above faces or main subjects (gap above as a fraction of frame height)?
questions.why_it_matters: Reveals where space is left for titles in vertical framing.
questions.how_to_answer: On keyframes with a face or subject, measure top of subject to top of frame / height.
questions.challenge: Check whether headroom is consistently occupied by the title; if so, say so.

questions.question: Are source images and clips shown full-bleed, inset with margins, letterboxed, or on a blurred fill?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides how assets of the wrong aspect are placed.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F1 frames per shot type; look for bars, margins or a blurred copy around the media.
questions.challenge: A blurred fill can look like a background video; check whether it mirrors the foreground.

questions.question: What fraction of the frame width does the main photo or clip occupy?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills frame_coverage of the main visual layer (a common house constraint is at least 80%).
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the main media's left and right edges on F1 frames in 5 shots; width / source.width.
questions.challenge: Feathered edges make the boundary soft; measure where opacity visibly reaches half.

questions.question: What kinds of visual material appear (filmed footage, photographs, screen recordings, illustrations, 3D renders, generated images, charts, maps)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills style_family and the asset types an author must source.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify each keyframe; list kinds with counts.
questions.challenge: Label 'generated images' only with a visible cue and mark it inferred; never as fact from style alone.

questions.question: How many distinct visual assets are used per item beat (median)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets assets_per_item for the content slot.
questions.how_to_answer: Within each item, group shots whose keyframes have SSIM above 0.7 (F10) as one asset; count groups.
questions.challenge: A zoomed crop of the same photo is one asset; check grouping by eye on one item.

questions.question: Is there an on-camera presenter or talking head, and what share of runtime is it on screen?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the format needs a presenter slot or a character layer.
questions.how_to_answer: Mark shots showing a person speaking to camera (mouth movement on F2 bursts aligned with speech); sum their durations / duration.
questions.challenge: Do not identify the person; answers containing identity are rejected.

questions.question: Does shot scale alternate between consecutive shots (wide then close, close then wide)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a scale alternation rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Using the shot types from 001, count consecutive pairs that change scale by at least one step.
questions.challenge: Graphic cards have no scale; exclude them from pairs.

questions.question: What share of factual claims are illustrated by a dedicated visual (B-roll that shows the thing being said)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets how literally visuals follow the script.
questions.how_to_answer: For 10 sampled caption cards, check whether the concurrent frame (F1) depicts the claim's subject.
questions.challenge: This is a judgement; method must be observed with the sample listed.

questions.question: Where does the framing leave negative space for text (top band, bottom band, side, none)?
questions.why_it_matters: Couples framing with typography placement.
questions.how_to_answer: Overlay evidence.text_regions[] bboxes on sampled frames mentally or with drawbox; check if text sits on low-detail areas.
questions.challenge: If text sits over the subject (a deliberate style), the answer is 'none'.

questions.question: Does the subject's gaze or direction of movement point toward the text or away from it?
questions.why_it_matters: A layout rule for composing subject and text.
questions.how_to_answer: On keyframes with faces or moving subjects, compare gaze or motion direction with the text position.
questions.challenge: Fewer than 4 qualifying shots means not determinable.

questions.question: How many images or clips are reused in more than one beat?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator whether reuse is allowed (asset budget).
questions.how_to_answer: Pairwise F10 SSIM between keyframes from different beats; count pairs above 0.8 that are the same asset.
questions.challenge: Template backgrounds produce high SSIM; compare the foreground region only (F3 crop) for flagged pairs.

questions.question: Do backgrounds behind subjects look optically or synthetically blurred (shallow depth of field)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a depth cue to the layer recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at subject edges: optical blur grows gradually with depth; synthetic blur shows a hard cut-out halo.
questions.challenge: Compression smearing is not blur; compare with a sharp region in the same frame.

questions.question: Are horizontal sources fitted into the vertical frame by recropping, by blurred fill bars, or by stacking?
questions.why_it_matters: Defines the aspect adapter step in the render plan.
questions.how_to_answer: Find shots where content aspect differs from the frame (F1); classify the method.
questions.challenge: Native vertical footage gives not-applicable; do not infer from one shot.

questions.question: How many diagrams, charts or maps appear, and are they built in-video (animated) or static images?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds chart or map layer kinds and their build method.
questions.how_to_answer: Mark keyframes with diagrams; inspect F2 bursts to see whether elements animate on.
questions.challenge: A photo of a chart is not an animated chart; check for element-level motion.

questions.question: What camera angle dominates (eye level, high angle, low angle, top-down, mixed)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an angle preference for asset selection or 3D rendering.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify sampled keyframes by apparent camera angle.
questions.challenge: Graphics and flat illustrations have no angle; exclude them.

questions.question: Does each item open with a wide or establishing shot before closer shots?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an item shot-order rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the scale of the first shot of each item with its later shots.
questions.challenge: Require at least two thirds of items to follow it.

questions.question: Are close-ups or tight crops used at the moments key numbers are revealed?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a 'tighten on reveal' rule.
questions.how_to_answer: At each key-number appearance (text_regions in the label or number area), compare shot scale with the item median.
questions.challenge: If numbers appear on graphic cards, the question does not apply; answer not determinable.

questions.question: Do inset media have borders, rounded corners, drop shadows or device frames?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds border or frame layers to the stack.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at inset corners; measure corner radius and border width in px.
questions.challenge: Report px measurements; 'rounded' without a radius is incomplete.

questions.question: How often are picture-in-picture or split-screen layouts used (share of runtime)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the compiler needs a multi-panel layout.
questions.how_to_answer: Sum durations of shots with two or more media panels (F1); divide by duration.
questions.challenge: Decorative background grids are not picture-in-picture.

questions.question: What minimum pixel width must a source asset have to fill the main visual slot without visible upscaling?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets min_asset_px for asset sourcing.
questions.how_to_answer: Main visual width in px (006) times the maximum zoom factor seen (camera lens answers or first/last frame comparison).
questions.challenge: Check one zoomed shot on an F3 crop for softness that shows the source was already upscaled.

questions.question: What shot slots does one item need (for example hero image, detail crop, context wide, number card)?
questions.why_it_matters: Defines the per-item shot list template.
questions.how_to_answer: From items, list the recurring shot roles in order; keep roles present in at least two thirds of items.
questions.challenge: Test the list on one item not used to build it.

questions.question: How consistent is subject scale across items (standard deviation of subject height ratio)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator whether to normalise subject size.
questions.how_to_answer: Using 002 measurements grouped by item, report the stdev of per-item medians.
questions.challenge: Report the number of items measured.

questions.question: What share of shots contain people (any visible person)?
questions.why_it_matters: Shapes asset sourcing and rights needs (model releases).
questions.how_to_answer: Count keyframes with a visible person; divide by shot count.
questions.challenge: Do not describe or identify people; count only.

questions.question: Are any shots tilted (dutch angle) or rotated in the frame?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds rotation as a framing device.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect keyframes for non-level horizons or rotated insets; measure the angle on F3 crops.
questions.challenge: Rotation from a camera move belongs to the camera lens; check whether the angle changes over the shot.

questions.question: Are shot changes matched on shape, colour or position (match cuts)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds match cuts to the editing toolbox.
questions.how_to_answer: For each cut, compare the subject position and dominant colour of adjacent frames (F1 before/after, F9 colours); list matches.
questions.challenge: Coincidental similarity is common in template videos; require deliberate alignment of the main subject.

questions.question: Is the main subject ever cropped by the frame edge, and is that systematic (tight crops) or accidental?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a crop policy.
questions.how_to_answer: Count keyframes where the subject touches or exceeds a frame edge.
questions.challenge: Report the count and total shots inspected.

questions.question: What share of shots are pure graphics (no photographic or filmed content)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the mix between sourced media and generated graphics.
questions.how_to_answer: Count graphic-only keyframes / total.
questions.challenge: A photo with heavy overlays is not a pure graphic.

questions.question: Which visual asset parameters must the author supply per item, with type and aspect (for example hero_image: asset, 9:16 or wider, at least 1600 px)?
questions.why_it_matters: Feeds the parameteriser with asset slots.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine 008, 023 and 024 into typed asset parameters.
questions.challenge: Every asset parameter needs a min size and aspect backed by a measurement.

questions.question: What rule picks the hero visual for an item (shows the subject named in the label, shows the key number's object, shows a person reacting)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the asset search step a selection rule.
questions.how_to_answer: For each item, compare the hero shot content with the item's label or key number (F1 plus F3 label crop).
questions.challenge: Check the rule against every item; exceptions must be listed.

questions.question: Is the frame divided by a consistent layout grid (fixed margins or columns that media and text align to)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a layout grid to the render binding.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure left and right edges of media and text across 6 frames; report repeated x positions within 1% of width.
questions.challenge: Centred elements always share an axis; require a shared edge, not just centring.
